TEAM WORKSPACE / DECISION BRIEFVersion 01

A useful next step.

Keep the current workspace for everyday work. Run a two-week pilot of the new approach with four volunteers.

Why this direction

The team values its familiar routines [1]. A small pilot lets us test the promising parts of the trial [2] while keeping the estimated setup effort contained [3].

What the evidence says

  • Continuity matters. Five of six people interviewed want to keep familiar daily workflows. [1]
  • There is something worth testing. The trial produced an adjustable checklist and a reusable planning template. [2]
  • Setup takes attention. Allow an estimated half day to prepare a pilot and orient volunteers. [3]
STILL AN OPEN QUESTION

Will the new workspace remain useful after the novelty wears off?

How we’ll learn

Ask each volunteer to bring one real task each week. Review the results together, including what was awkward or unfinished.

THE EVIDENCE

Keep the sources
in the conversation.

These three notes are fictional material created for this example.

01 · Team interviews

Six people were interviewed. Five preferred to preserve their familiar routines. Three were curious about making small tools for work they repeat. This small sample does not establish what the whole team will prefer.

02 · Trial notes

A short trial produced an adjustable checklist and a planning template. Participants found editing the result useful, but needed help with the first setup. Longer-term use was not measured.

03 · Setup estimate

The pilot organizer estimated half a day to prepare the workspace, configure access, and orient four volunteers. This is a planning estimate, not measured time or a price quote.
